_README: The offices this site does not track the votes of: the Governor, the five
Executive Councillors, the two members of the US House and the two US
Senators. None of them appear in any General Court file, which is where
everything else on Granite Record comes from.
THIS FILE IS EDITED BY HAND AND NO GENERATOR WRITES IT, for the same
reason ground_truth.csv is: a name against an office is a claim about a
real person holding real power, and it must come from somebody who
checked rather than from a build step that guessed.
Every record carries the page it was read from and the date it was read.
These offices change at an election; when one does, the names here are
stale and the official_url is still right, which is why the page links to
it either way.
PARTY IS RECORDED ONLY WHERE A SOURCE STATED IT, AND THE SOURCE IS NAMED.
senate.gov gives a party for each senator. governor.nh.gov,
council.nh.gov and the members' own house.gov sites do not, so those
eight were blank until 12 September 2026, when the site's author
supplied them: Ayotte R, Kenney R, Liot Hill D, Stevens R, Stephen R,
Wheeler R, Pappas D, Goodlander D. That is a person's statement rather
than a page's, which is the whole reason this file is a person's file.
A party chip is a visible claim about a real person; if one of these is
wrong, it is wrong here and nowhere else.
SINCE 9 OCTOBER 2026, ALSO THE SECRETARY OF STATE, THE STATE TREASURER AND
THE ATTORNEY GENERAL, read that day from each office's own pages, whose
addresses each record carries. The person approved the three names in chat
the same day. None of the three pages states a party, so none is recorded.
The Secretary of State and the Treasurer are elected by the General Court
for each biennium, so both are read again after the new General Court
chooses them in December.
SINCE 9 OCTOBER 2026, ALSO EACH COUNTY'S ELECTED OFFICERS (key county): its
three commissioners, sheriff, county attorney, treasurer, register of deeds
and register of probate, 80 in all, read from the Secretary of State's county
roster (records/sources/sos-county-roster-2025-2026.pdf, dated 5 December
2024). The person approved them in chat the same day and decided that a
commissioner carries the party the roster prints (R/D where a candidate won
both nominations, shown on a neutral chip), while the sheriff, county attorney,
treasurer and the two registers carry none: their roles are meant to be
neutral, as a Secretary of State's is. Most of these seats are on the November
2026 ballot, so every name is read again from the next roster.

governor.name: Kelly Ayotte
about: As the head of state government, the Governor signs or vetoes legislation passed in the General Court, oversees state agencies, and proposes the state budget for legislative approval.
Five councilors, elected from five districts. The Executive Council approves state contracts over $10,000, judicial and agency nominations, and pardons.
New Hampshire elects two members of the US House, one from each congressional district.
us_house.source: https://www.sos.nh.gov/congressional-delegation, and each member's own site for the district

2.name: Maggie Goodlander
2.source: https://goodlander.house.gov/about states New Hampshire's Second District

about: Two senators, elected by the whole state, so both represent every town.

secretary_of_state.name: David M. Scanlan
about: As chief election official, the Secretary of State oversees all state elections. The office also keeps the state's corporations, securities, archives and vital records. The Secretary is elected by a joint session of the House and Senate.

treasurer.name: Monica Mezzapelle
about: The State Treasurer oversees the state's finances, including investments and debt management. Part 2, Article 67 of the New Hampshire Constitution establishes the office, and the Treasurer is elected by a joint session of the Senate and the House.

attorney_general.name: John Formella
about: The Attorney General is the State's chief legal officer and chief law enforcement officer, and heads the Department of Justice.
Each of New Hampshire's ten counties elects three county commissioners, a sheriff, a county attorney, a county treasurer, a register of deeds and a register of probate.

Each commissioner represents a district (in Carroll and Sullivan the whole county votes for each one). In eight counties their terms are staggered, so two of the three seats are on the ballot at each general election; Hillsborough and Strafford elect all three every two years. The other officers serve two-year terms, except in Rockingham and Coos, where they serve four.
When an office falls vacant between elections, the county convention -- the county's state representatives -- fills it; a register of probate's vacancy is filled differently.
